title: Launch the Executive MBA & Leadership Mastermind Cohort Operations Pack for Business Schools, by Fri 11 Dec
description:
Executive MBA programs, corporate academies, and high-ticket leadership masterminds ($3,000–$15,000 tuition per participant) require a premium, distraction-free digital home. Senior executives and founders refuse to join chaotic public chat apps and expect white-glove privacy, structured syndicate study rooms, and executive guest speaker sessions. This blueprint positions Zedu as the premier executive learning workspace for elite business institutions.

Work under this goal:
- Architect the closed executive syndicate workspace model: private 5-person executive mastermind pods (#syndicate-alpha, #syndicate-beta), faculty advisory channels, and VIP guest speaker lounges.
- Author the Executive Fireside protocol for live guest-CEO Q&A sessions using native Zedu Buzz calls with muted audience controls and speaker spotlighting.
- Design the executive case study deliberation thread protocol using Zedu's 440px side drawer for asynchronous board-room simulations and pitch critiques.
- Create an executive slide and confidential financial model repository architecture using Zedu File Management's restricted per-file view links.

Done when: An executive cohort operations kit is delivered complete with VIP invitation copy, syndicate group formation rules, boardroom deliberation templates, and verified zedu-fe permission setups for high-security corporate programs.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Make every executive session declare a confidentiality tier and a recording rule before it starts
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The pack promises a distraction-free executive home, but it does not say which conversations may be recorded, transcribed or reused. Approach: define three tiers - five-person pod, faculty advisory, and plenary or fireside - and for each state who may invite, who may read files, whether audio or video may be recorded, and what the host must announce before the session. Default to no recording; any recording needs named consent from every participant and one agreed storage location. Done: a one-page tier card, a pre-session announcement script, a four-line host checklist, and an audit query that lists sessions with no declared tier. Measured: every session declares a tier before it starts, zero unapproved recordings at the first monthly audit, and the goal owner signs off the tiers. Why it fits: executives paying $3,000-$15,000 will ask who can hear and replay them; session-level rules turn the white-glove promise into an operating control.

upvotes.reason: "Make every executive session declare a confidentiality tier and a recording rule before it starts" has a scriptable structure, so it can be produced and reviewed rather than left open-ended. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

This sets clear privacy expectations for executive sessions, including a no-recording default, a participant-consent rule and a host announcement before the session. The proposed audit should be a manual checklist unless the product is verified to support a session-level audit; that keeps the pack from implying controls Zedu may not have.

An executive programme cannot promise a distraction-free space without saying what may be recorded and who may read it. Three tiers with named permissions is the minimum a faculty member will ask about before speaking freely.
Enforcing explicit confidentiality tiers and recording permissions is essential for executive MBA cohorts handling sensitive corporate data.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.

tasks.title: Draft the executive session confidentiality tier card, announcement script and host checklist

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Verify every privacy promise made to executives against the product before the pack claims "white-glove privacy"
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Executives will ask who can read their DMs, whether admins can export conversations, where data is stored and how a member is removed cleanly. Approach: answer each question from the current product, privacy policy and team confirmation, mark unknowns, and write the pack's privacy section only from verified answers. Then design the syndicate rooms using private channels and guest access for speakers where the product supports them. Done: the privacy Q&A with sources, the verified feature list for the pack, and the claims removed or changed because they couldn't be verified.

upvotes.reason: "Verify every privacy promise made to executives against the product before the pack claims "white-glove privacy"" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.
Verifying who can read DMs and export conversations before claiming white-glove privacy keeps the pack from promising something the product does not do.

This is a strong trust safeguard for an executive-cohort pack: it asks the team to verify access, export, storage and removal behavior, mark unknowns, and remove unsupported privacy claims before publication. The room design is conditional on confirmed product controls.

An executive pack claiming white-glove privacy must answer who can read DMs and export conversations from the product, not from aspiration. Verifying first and removing unsupported claims is the right order.
Executives will ask who can read a DM and where data is stored. Verifying each promise before the pack claims privacy is the only defensible order.
